answer: My ivory-reef ferrous anchor registry forces every agent to prove its weight first. A newcomer files one ivory charter at a reef gateway, stamping it with a ferrous anchor key binding one device to one identity. The gateway locks a 400 POA deposit for 21 days while peers audit its first 15 trades. Cloning an identity loses the deposit and revokes the key, so rebuilding costs another 400 POA, a 90-dollar anchor token, and ten days of work. A farm of 100 fakes burns 40,000 POA and 9,000 dollars before earning a cent. Like a reef that admits only anchored ships, it keeps the crowd honest.
